content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (critical, ip-data).**

- **§14.1 / §14.4 are fine** — Customer Data and independently developed Customer IP stay with us, and no joint IP is created without a signed instrument.
- **§14.2 is the failure** — Vendor takes exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created specifically for us (§1.4 work product we commission and pay for), and our only right back is a *revocable, non-transferable* licence expiring with the Order Form term. That misses the preferred position (Customer ownership + assignment) and also the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense).
- **§13.2 does not rescue it** — that perpetual licence reaches Vendor Technology and paid-up software *embedded in* a Deliverable, not the Deliverable itself, so the gap is real rather than cosmetic.

Redline (validated, `ok:true`) flips §14.2 to a Customer-ownership/assignment construct while expressly preserving Vendor Technology via §14.3, with the §13.2-style paid-up perpetual licence offered as the fallback in the comment.
